entry_thesis: Target has been left for dead by Wall Street — down 40% from 5-year highs — yet just reported Q4 EPS of $2.44 vs $2.15 consensus (13.5% beat) with multiple analyst upgrades (Telsey to Outperform PT $145, Bernstein, Citigroup, UBS, Goldman) arriving March 4. At ~$120 the stock trades at only 15x 2026 guided EPS of $7.50-$8.50, a historically cheap multiple for a dominant blue-chip retailer executing a genuine turnaround with a new CEO, $5B capex plan, and 30+ new stores in 2026. Middle East geopolitical fears and tariff anxiety are hammering consumer discretionary broadly — creating the perfect cover for the market to underprice TGT's improving fundamentals and accelerating analyst re-rating.
risk: Consumer sentiment cratered to 53.3 and tariff-driven cost inflation could squeeze margins further; if the macro environment deteriorates sharply, TGT's discretionary exposure makes it a laggard even at cheap valuations.
catalyst: Wave of analyst upgrades and price target increases triggers institutional FOMO; Q1 2026 earnings (May) expected to show traffic recovery confirming the turnaround thesis; Middle East de-escalation removes macro overhang on consumer discretionary sector.
